verdicts.claim: Never call the project 'open source' (at most 'open-source code', only under licence shape A or C); CLAUDE.md's public 'Free and open source' must be fixed.
verdicts.what_is_true: The repo is public with no licence (GitHub API license null, no LICENSE file), yet CLAUDE.md:3 says 'Free and open source', which is false under the OSI definition. README.md:7 correctly says all rights reserved and the live pages never say open source; vision.md:79 is a planned README line held for the licence, not a published claim. Harm is small because the README contradicts it.
external: https://opensource.org/osd (accessed 2026-11-07): 'The distribution terms of open source software must comply with the following criteria'
verdicts.fix: Change CLAUDE.md:3 to 'free to play; licence not chosen' now, rather than waiting for the licence pick; keep the rule.

verdicts.claim: Store and marketing copy claims only what a visitor can do on the live build, checked on the day and reviewed by Legal, with the six RL-094 edits; controller, fighter-count, mode, open-source, trademark and Steam Deck claims held.
verdicts.what_is_true: The live holding page follows the edits (computer-controlled opponent, procedural clarifier, privacy line, 'in development'), and its beam-trench and building-stage claims are real in pin 257a766c. The unreviewed claims (H10, P10, P13) sit only in unpublished drafts. But the public README, which this review process does not cover, misstates the live build: line 7 says the hosted build is offline while /play/ returns 200, and line 9 still says 'We are fixing them'.
external: https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/basics/what-trademark (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Once you register your trademark with us, use an ® with the trademark.'
verdicts.fix: Keep the rule, and add the README to the copy it covers: correct README.md:7 (a test build is up behind a notice) and README.md:9 (drop 'We are fixing them').

verdicts.claim: Promotion hold until the title is decided and Legal reviews each asset; holding page noindex, no social card, logo or links by the project, AI line near the top; clips as video, no autoplay or loop, analyser pass, no title or personal data in frame.
verdicts.what_is_true: The live / page (fetched today, byte-identical to the saved copy) has noindex, '(working title)', the AI line near the top, and no og or twitter tags, images or links; no clip is published on the site. The repo's own homepage field links to the Pages site, a small gap against 'no links by us'. Off-site posts and outreach were not checked. The hold is partly business strategy (avoiding promotion before a rename); its legal kernel is the title clash.
verdicts.fix: Keep the hold. Remove the repo homepage link (or record it as accepted) and keep the clip conditions for when a clip exists.

verdicts.claim: The live pin may keep its old in-game notice ('We are fixing them', untrue while flash work is paused) until the pin moves or 2026-11-08; a strings-only child is due by 2026-11-08, else the excuse rides once to 2026-11-15 with Orb told.
verdicts.what_is_true: The pin's photo_body_a and menu_notice both say 'We are fixing them', the excuse runs to 2026-11-08, and no strings-only child commit exists. The stale promise does not weaken the warning, which still tells photosensitive players not to play. The waiver's machinery is moot: with ci.yml failing, neither the expiry check nor a child or take-down can deploy. README.md:9 carries the same stale line, outside the waiver.
verdicts.fix: Record that the 2026-11-08 child cannot ship while CI is dead, tell Orb the line is stale as RL-209 requires, and fix README.md:9 at the same time.

verdicts.claim: The neutral position-diamond glyphs will probably fail Steam Deck Verified, so the Deck uses Steam Input glyphs or plain lettered Deck/Xbox glyphs, with no PlayStation symbols; claim nothing about Steam Deck until Valve awards a badge.
verdicts.what_is_true: Valve's checklist says on-screen glyphs must match the input (Deck, Steam Controller or Xbox glyphs), as go-to-market.md:248 states. The default style in ui/data/glyphs.json is NEUTRAL (S/E/W/N in a diamond), with a lettered 'family' style present but off, so a Deck review would likely fail it. The trademark side is already handled: the ps family uses S/E/W/N, and no Deck claim appears on the live pages. Failing Verified costs a rating, not player safety.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamdeck/compat (accessed 2026-11-07): 'On-screen glyphs must match the inputs being used'
verdicts.fix: Keep it parked for the Steam build: turn on the family style for Deck and Xbox pads, or use Steam Input glyphs; it is a platform-certification task for Controls more than a safety item.
verdicts.belongs_to: Controls (glyphs); Legal (console marks and the badge claim)

verdicts.claim: Steam readiness: $100 non-refundable fee, bank, tax and identity checks with names matching the legal ID, about 30 days plus a two-week Coming Soon page, AI survey pre-generated yes and live no, SDK never committed, nothing past the fee until the title search and licence are done.
verdicts.what_is_true: Valve's pages confirm the $100 fee (not refundable, recoupable at $1,000), the legal-ID name match, the 15-30 day verification, the two-week Coming Soon page and the pre-generated/live AI categories. No Steamworks SDK file is tracked. One correction: Steam Direct and Onboarding both say 21 days today, so the record's line that Steam Direct says 30 is out of date (planning on 30 is a harmless margin). Most items are business logistics; the legal kernel is the AI survey and keeping the SDK out of the public repo.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect (accessed 2026-11-07): 'A 21-day waiting period between when you paid the app fee'
https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey (accessed 2026-11-07): 'created with the help of AI tools during development'
verdicts.fix: Correct A3 to say Valve now states 21 days on both pages and that 30 is a margin. Move the fee, tax and wait items to Marketing's readiness half and keep the AI survey and SDK items with Legal.
verdicts.belongs_to: Legal (AI survey, SDK); Orb's business calls; Community & Marketing (logistics)

verdicts.claim: No tips, sales or promotion before the licence, title and Suno plan are settled; a lawyer's single sitting before the first sale covers title clearance, licence texts, AI warranties, tax and business status, a privacy policy and the nemesis patent.
verdicts.what_is_true: The gate is in force: there is no FUNDING.yml and no tip, price or sale wording in the README or on the live pages. The patent is real and active: US 10,926,179 (Warner Bros, granted 2021-02-23, adjusted expiry 2036-08-11 per Google Patents). The title clash is still open. Whether the campaign mechanic reads on the patent claims was not checked. The patent is in steam-readiness.md:52 but missing from go-to-market.md:19's lawyer list.
external: https://patents.google.com/patent/US10926179B2/en (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Nemesis characters, nemesis forts, social vendettas and followers in computer games'
verdicts.fix: Keep the gate; add the patent question to go-to-market.md:19's list so the lawyer list is one list.

verdicts.claim: Licence shape A fits Steam. Steamworks and console SDK terms are addressed in an addendum.
verdicts.what_is_true: The inventory is wrong that no source is given: the addendum at go-to-market.md:239-245 cites Valve's open-source page. That page lists MIT as acceptable and copyleft as problematic, so shape A (MIT code) fits. The console SDK terms are behind NDA and unverified, as Legal itself says.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/uploading/distributing_opensource (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Common permissive and acceptable licenses includes MIT License'
verdicts.fix: Correct the inventory note (the source exists); leave the console part as a lawyer item.

verdicts.claim: Reduce flashing lock wording passes once the 'at most one large flash a second' claim is dropped; a flag check in the interim export is a condition.
verdicts.what_is_true: Both conditions are met: the 'one large flash a second' claim appears in no pin string or live page, and the live gate carries Legal's lock line word for word. The interim export sets lock_reduce_flashing true (site-pin.mjs:85-91; the pin's committed features.json:12 has it false) and check-site-interim.mjs:357 fails a build without it. RL-157's 'Open' status is stale. The deployed package itself was not inspected.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-157 and cite the export step and the check as the evidence.

verdicts.claim: Interim without a signature close-up: page copy must not describe it, and it is measured under full effects when the toggle returns.
verdicts.what_is_true: The premise is stale: the signature strip was dropped under Reduce flashing on 2026-10-17 (e8d91dea) and restored on 2026-10-19 (10267f51), before the pin. In 257a766c, panel_flash_off is [] and camera panels default to full, so the live interim does show the signature close-up. Neither page mentions it either way (no match on / or /play/), and the 'when the toggle returns' measurement was triggered on 2026-10-19.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: an open row waits on a page-text check that no longer matters, and readers are told the live demo lacks a close-up it has, which hides that its return needed its own flash reading.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: the strip came back in 10267f51, before the pin. Close the copy half, and tie the measurement half to the pin's recorded signature-clip readings (RL-209) or write that test.

verdicts.claim: Public text, tags and handles never use franchise words, fan-game names or our working names, relationship words (tribute, parody, clone, homage, 'for fans of') or unsupported claim words (human-made, no AI, balanced, official, registered, Steam Deck Verified before the badge).
verdicts.what_is_true: The live pages, the repo description and the topics use none of the banned words. The README uses the allowed genre phrase once, and README.md:7 names the codename 'Meridian', although the README is outside the list's stated scope. The ® and Deck rules rest on real USPTO and Valve rules. 'Balanced' and 'fair' are a margin, not law. The list does write franchise words into a public file, which Legal itself flagged at store-copy-screen.md:46; that is low risk because it is analysis, not use in trade.
external: https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/basics/what-trademark (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Once you register your trademark with us, use an ® with the trademark.'
verdicts.fix: Keep the rule; decide whether the README counts as public text for the working-name ban, and say so in the list.

verdicts.claim: Pages hosted on GitHub (the repo and Pages) follow GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies: no gratuitous graphic violence and no sales-led copy.
verdicts.what_is_true: GitHub's rules are correctly stated in p01: AUP section 2 (gratuitous violence) and section 10 (no advertising as the primary focus), and Pages may not host a business or shop. The live / page has no images, prices or sales copy. The game on /play/ was not played (no browsers in this audit), so its imagery was not checked.
external: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-acceptable-use-policies (accessed 2026-11-07): 'gratuitously depicts or glorifies violence, including violent images'
https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits (accessed 2026-11-07): 'not intended for or allowed to be used as a free web-hosting service'
verdicts.fix: Add the two URLs to p01 in place of 'read 2026-10-12'; no other work.

verdicts.claim: Nothing paid may give a random or hidden reward without asking Legal. Tips wait for the licence, the title and the Suno plan, carry no perks, and show the AI statement.
verdicts.what_is_true: Nothing is sold: there is no purchase, microtransaction or loot-box code in the shipped folders and no tip route on the public pages. The gambling concern is real (Belgium's Gaming Commission ruled paid loot boxes gambling in 2018, per secondary sources), but the record cites no law. The tips half duplicates AC-205.
external: Belgian Gaming Commission 2018 loot-box report: primary site gamingcommission.be not reached on 2026-11-07; only secondary coverage and a law-firm-hosted copy were found
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a standing guard; merge the tips half into AC-205's gate.

verdicts.claim: A store build needs a take-down plan and an email address someone reads. On any claim or demand: stop, do not reply, tell Orb and the EP, get counsel. A seizure report means a lawyer reads the warning and the records.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is sound, and the DMCA facts in tribute-vs-parody.md:14 match GitHub's policy. But its premise that 'the demo's kill switch exists' (steam-readiness.md:54) fails today: site-offline.mjs publishes only by commit and push through ci.yml, the last three ci.yml runs failed, and the last Pages deploy was 72a4d1e4 on 2026-11-05. No manual unpublish route is documented, and no read email exists; reports can only reach the project through GitHub issues or clipboard feedback.
verdicts.fix: Now: write and test an owner-run take-down that does not need CI (GitHub Settings > Pages, or the Pages DELETE endpoint), and fix ci.yml. Before store: set up a read contact address. Correct steam-readiness.md:54.

batch_notes: The public README misstates the live build in two places that no claim in this slice owns: README.md:7 says the hosted build is offline (/play/ returns 200), and README.md:9 still says 'We are fixing them', which is outside the in-game string excuse.
RL-160 (AC-208) is stale: the signature strip came back under Reduce flashing on 2026-10-19 (10267f51), before pin 257a766c.
The documented kill switch (tools/site-offline.mjs) depends on the dead ci.yml. No manual unpublish route is written down, though GitHub's Pages DELETE endpoint and the Settings page exist.
Valve's Steam Direct and Onboarding pages both say 21 days today, not 30 (AC-204).

The pin's committed features.json has lock_reduce_flashing false; the lock comes from the export step (site-pin.mjs), which the dead CI cannot run on any new deploy. The deployed package was not inspected.
The repo's homepage field links to the Pages site, a small gap against 'no links by us' (AC-201).
